---
title: "How Current Conversations will work"
description: "Planned methods, safeguards and limitations for Current Conversations."
---

<p class="status-badge in-development">In development</p>

<p class="page-deck">New work appears in journals, public reports, news, city networks and public discussion. Current Conversations is designed to connect some of that work to the lab’s four questions while keeping every original source visible.</p>

Current Conversations is not yet a live public feed. If it is enabled later, it will provide selective horizon scanning: a way to notice emerging discussions, not a validated evidence base, systematic review, quality assessment, recommendation, transferability assessment or complete map.

## Where material may be found

Bounded, versioned searches may check academic indexes and, only when separately authorised, current web material and public social-media sources. The system calls these places `source environments` and records the role each source plays. A peer-reviewed study, official announcement and news report do not provide the same kind of evidence.

Coverage will remain selective, incomplete and shaped by indexing, platform access, language and geography. English-language and well-indexed sources are likely to be overrepresented. This limitation will be stated wherever entries eventually appear.

## Evidence access and source integrity

Every record will retain the original source, publication date, stable identifier where available, retrieval date and actual evidence accessed. Titles and snippets will not support findings claims. Full copyrighted articles, paywalled text and raw provider payloads will not be stored in public records.

Source content will be treated as untrusted data. Embedded instructions will not be allowed to alter prompts, policy, budgets, repository behaviour or publication decisions.

## How records may be classified, grouped and summarised

AI may propose a theme, summary or connection between records. Deterministic controls must then check required fields and evidence. Grouping begins with DOI and other stable identifiers, canonical URLs, links to the same underlying source, explicit citations, platform identifiers, and matching title-and-organisation evidence. A bounded model may propose a pair, but independent evidence must accept it. Topic similarity or model confidence alone is insufficient.

Public disclosure will follow each record’s actual provenance. A record will claim AI assistance only when its provenance says AI was used. Original sources will remain authoritative, and disagreement or uncertainty will be retained rather than averaged away.

## Publication, review and corrections

Staging writes and public feeds remain disabled. A later launch decision will require validation, allowed-path controls, budget controls where paid services are involved, and explicit owner approval. Inclusion will not indicate endorsement, evidential quality or applicability to a particular city. Human-review badges will appear only when a named review actually occurred.

The [public correction route](../contact.qmd) will accept factual corrections, grouping concerns, broken-source reports and removal requests. Correction and merge/split history will remain traceable.
